# Plan the strategy of a product

## Directives

From [Product strategy](../../references/product-strategy.md):

- State the user problem of each feature in one sentence. ^state-user-problem
- Write the success measure of each feature before you build the feature. ^write-success-measure

From [Strategy formulation](../../references/strategy-formulation.md):

- In each strategy, name the goals and the work that the strategy sets aside. ^name-what-strategy-sets-aside
- Replace each buzzword in a strategy with the plain term that it stands for. ^remove-strategy-fluff
- Do not label a vision, a mission, or a values statement as a strategy. ^vision-is-not-strategy

From [Product measurement](../../references/product-measurement.md):

- Link each metric to the goal that it tracks. ^metric-tracks-a-goal
- Normalize each raw count to a ratio, a percentage, or an average for each user, unless it counts new users. ^prefer-normalized-metrics

From [Prioritization](../../references/product-prioritization.md):

- Give each product team business objectives with key results, not a list of features to build. ^objectives-not-feature-lists

From [Product positioning](../../references/product-positioning.md):

- Do not start positioning work from a fill-in positioning statement. ^no-fill-in-statement
- Write the positioning of a product before you write its messaging. ^positioning-before-messaging

## Required reads

Read each file in this list, and follow the directives that its line names.

- Read [Digital product development](../../references/digital-product-development.md), and follow each directive from Digital product development.
